rows.summary: CoreWeave’s neocloud thesis materially redirects but remains 4/5: falling cost per unit of intelligence can make deployed GPUs more economically valuable and premium software/reliability supports higher margins, but long-term winners must evolve from spot GPU rental toward optimized inference and token services.

SemiAnalysis Capital’s decision to co-lead TeRAM’s $37M seed is a high-conviction bet that inference’s memory-bandwidth and power wall can support a new 3D SRAM memory layer integrated directly onto AI compute chips rather than relying only on larger HBM stacks.

Nvidia’s platform thesis re-strengthens to 5/5 because Rubin’s first verified agentic-inference results show a large next-generation performance/TCO and power-efficiency lead while Nvidia’s day-zero model support continues to demonstrate the practical CUDA/software moat that competitors still struggle to match.

AMD’s AI-accelerator thesis weakens back to 3/5 because recent selective MI355X TCO wins have not yet generalized into a robust production-software moat: on the new DeepSeekV4.1 Flash release AMD lagged Nvidia on day-zero support and remained dramatically worse on current performance per dollar.

SK Hynix’s HBM thesis partially re-strengthens because SemiAnalysis’s new 4-hi analysis argues shorter HBM stacks can improve dollar-per-bandwidth, stacking yield and supplier profitability per scarce DRAM wafer, offsetting part of the prior margin concern even though Hynix’s company-specific HBM4 leadership and Nvidia bargaining-power issues remain.

Bloom’s behind-the-meter AI-power thesis materially re-strengthens: despite reciprocating engines remaining the broad share leader, Bloom now owns essentially all tracked fuel-cell bookings and is winning large deployments because its low-NOx, labor-light, vertically integrated fuel-cell model can clear permitting and execution bottlenecks that combustion equipment cannot.

SemiAnalysis’s reciprocating-engine thesis materially strengthens: behind-the-meter AI power has moved from early deployments to a 75GW firm-order market, recips continue gaining share as turbine slots push beyond 2030, and Caterpillar is nearly tripling large-engine output while 24/7 prime-power duty creates a recurring service cycle.

GE Vernova remains a strong turbine-scarcity beneficiary, but SemiAnalysis’s current BTM work redirects the thesis: factory slots now extend past 2030 and secondary-market premiums confirm exceptional scarcity pricing, while faster-growing recip and fuel-cell suppliers are capturing more of the marginal datacenter-specific volume.

Dylan Patel is making a direct high-conviction bet that AI inference is becoming memory-bound enough for Positron’s memory-first architecture to create a major alternative accelerator platform by using commodity LPDDR5X to bypass HBM and advanced-packaging bottlenecks.

Google’s merchant TPU/GCP thesis materially strengthens again: third-party InferenceX preview results now show TPUv7 Ironwood can beat Nvidia B200/B300 on modeled inference performance per dollar across meaningful FP8 operating points while Google rapidly externalizes its software stack, materially de-risking the technical foundation behind SemiAnalysis’s already-bullish external TPU/GCP revenue thesis.

OpenAI’s 5/5 thesis strengthens again: model-driven serving optimization is directly lowering inference cost while its custom-ASIC program has asymmetric strategic value—successful Jalapeño raises revenue per MW, while even failure can extract substantial Nvidia financing and backstops.

Anthropic’s thesis materially strengthens: SemiAnalysis expects Anthropic and OpenAI to absorb roughly half of incremental global AI compute by end-2027 and potentially 70–80% by 2028 because frontier-lab revenue per MW lets them economically outbid other buyers.

Broadcom’s custom-AI-silicon thesis materially strengthens because OpenAI’s first-generation Jalapeño ASIC, built with Broadcom, is already a credible high-volume Rubin-class inference competitor, validating Broadcom’s ability to monetize frontier labs’ shift from merchant GPUs toward custom accelerators.

Cerebras materially strengthens its ultra-low-latency inference proposition with CS-4, nearly doubling per-user token speed at roughly similar customer TCO while improving rack manufacturability and enabling heterogeneous disaggregated inference.

SemiAnalysis still believes SpaceX can scale AI compute toward 10GW by year-end 2027 and monetize scarce capacity at exceptional pricing, but its current published base case points to roughly $300B of ARR rather than the $500B figure previously captured in the ledger.

Vertiv is positioned to roughly double its revenue content per datacenter megawatt as AI builders shift from component purchases toward integrated modular power, cooling and facility platforms that materially shorten construction schedules.
ASML is entering a stronger multiyear wafer-fab-equipment upcycle, with improving visibility, pricing and installed-base economics creating upside to consensus revenue and likely long-term guidance.

Meta still has unusual advantages in data, talent, compute and distribution, but infrastructure politics and repeated hardware co-design failures materially reduce confidence that its enormous capex will translate efficiently into frontier-model and external-compute returns.
TSMC’s advanced-node capacity is becoming the central AI-silicon bottleneck, supporting exceptional utilization, customer dependence and pricing power.
